Not published.** Matt Dell · Council · incumbent (held City office 2022–26). Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. Duplicate of the template, renamed once. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom and is Joa's to apply or reject. Incumbent rule: Record in the cell; sourced miss caps below Close (max Partial+ 1.5). Alignment compute APPLIED letter for Dell stays **D**. ## Card

### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **record** Named YES on the 7 May 2026 budget (7.28 overall / 9.34 residential). "They want to protect the things that we love in the city." No cap, formula or glide path. The 2023–25 "lowest of most surrounding cities" line is a comparative frame, not a restraint rule. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026
Downtown order M26 / M27 **record** Campaign Record page: started OUR DWTN (cleanliness, safety, events) and supported the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan. No Public Order Team and no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. 2026 "keep investing in community safety and wellbeing" is scored nowhere as M26/M27. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) · [https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/](https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/) retrieved 2026-09-02 · launch 31 Dec 2025
Housing M6 **said** "We need to get back on track and speed up new rental, affordable, social and market housing. I commit to making that happen as soon as possible." No unit target and no 25/20/15 mix. Record: named YES on Missing Middle, 26 Jan 2023. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. — —
Written program — **yes** Authorized 2026 re-election site with a policies page (eight themes) plus a Record page. Directional, not costed, no tax formula, no permit benchmark, no dashboard, no \$25M threshold. [https://www.mattdell.ca/](https://www.mattdell.ca/) · [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics No topic gets its own letter. Area columns stay blank. Rules as written on . Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date**. A dash is unknown, not a fail. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Partial 1.0** "We need to get back on track and speed up new rental, affordable, social and market housing. I commit to making that happen as soon as possible." · Commits to a supply mix with no unit target and no composition share. Record, matching, not a second mark: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023 ("Council members in favour of the program — Jeremy Caradonna, Dave Thompson, Susan Kim, Krista Loughton, Matt Dell and Mayor Marianne Alto"). Family Housing Policy / 3-bedroom incentive on the Record page is the same supply cell, not a second mark. Not a sourced miss, so no Close cap. The 9,000-units figure is campaign-attributed, not an ACTW number, and is not stamped. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-council-adopts-divisive-missing-middle-housing-program-6443676) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — Non-market / rental acceleration is scored on row 1. No City land bank, acquisition fund or co-op financing. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening — Missing Middle's staff-level permits sit inside the vote already scored on row 1. No permit-time standard, nothing on AI pre-screening. One sentence, one measure. — —
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs do not appear. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Reduced development cost charges for affordable housing by 100%." No named Dell yes/no opened this pass. No 2026 vacancy target or suite amnesty. Shown, not scored. Do not invent a roll-call. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No unified command, co-location or downtown operations desk. CSWB and OUR DWTN are not a Public Order Team. Launch "keep investing in community safety and wellbeing" is a Mention of safety with no POT instrument, so a dash. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — No CRCL / IMCRT / civilian dispatched-response position. Harm-reduction language on the Record page is health-side, not a crisis-response team. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours or staffing number. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement — No position on targeting chronic disorder drivers with data. — —
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws — No 2026 bylaw-enforcement sentence. FLAG: Times Colonist 19 Jul 2024 names Kim as "the lone vote against" stepped-up daytime sheltering, 8–1. Dell is not named. Do not invent a roll-call. — —
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — Buffer zones and child-focused spaces do not appear. Harm reduction on the Record page is not a buffer bylaw. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Ended sheltering in Topaz, Stadacona, Vic West, Irving, Central, Hollywood and Beacon Hill park by hiring a Housing Relocation Coordinator to work with people to find suitable homes." No 2026 continue-sentence and no named Dell yes/no opened this pass. Shown, not scored. Night lighting is not named. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Opposed −1.0** "Voting for the budget were councillors Matt Dell, Jeremy Caradonna, Chris Coleman, Dave Thompson, Krista Loughton and Mayor Marianne Alto." Adopted 7.28 overall / 9.34 residential. Disagrees with a residential-rate cap. Context, same debate, not a second mark: "They want to protect the things that we love in the city." / "If you want to cut the budget, put forward programs people love." 2026 policies are silent on a cap. The 2023–25 "lowest municipal tax increase of most surrounding major cities" claim is a comparative frame, not a restraint instrument, and is not scored here. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-passes-budget-in-debate-that-hints-at-start-of-election-campaign-12259094) · [https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/city-budget) vote 7 May 2026 / press 9 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — No over-collection refund, no debt rule, no supermajority override. Budget-vote sentence is scored on row 13. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — Water, sewer, stormwater and the combined household number do not appear. "Tackling affordability" on the home page is housing and business, scored on rows 1 and 18. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger — No published downloading ledger and no refusal threshold. Province-blaming as a frame is not a source (same exclusion as the live profile / grade-breakdown note). — —
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — Regional water rates and the filtration plant do not appear. CREST / Harbour Authority seats are seats held, not a source. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Partial 1.0** "More supports for local business and tourism." · Commits to downtown-business support with no vacancy target and no one-mandate-not-a-new-office. Record page downtown tax-reduction / facade / Douglas funds are matching context, not a second mark. OUR DWTN cleanliness is row 26. [https://www.mattdell.ca/](https://www.mattdell.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No 15-minute grace, no capital-approval threshold, no permit-fee schedule. First-hour is not a Year-1 instrument. Crystal Pool is scored on row 39, not as a threshold rule. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. **Partial 1.0** "I support the City's commitment to Reconciliation with the Esquimalt and Songhees Nation, and will work collaboratively with local First Nations to implement the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Calls to Action." · Commits to a City TRC-implementation action. No standing government-to-government table, no procurement target, no place-name programme, no urban Indigenous liaison. The homepage lək̓ʷəŋan acknowledgement is not a second mark. Professional / volunteer background is not a source. Record-page PEERS Indigenous-led return programme is not this Foundation package and is not scored here. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Partial 1.0** "To do this, we must accelerate construction of non-market housing, build thousands of new rental units, and strengthen policies to protect renters." · Commits to renter-protection policy. Neither: no demoviction bylaw named, no STR licensing, no indoor-heat standard in the 2026 sentence. Housing-supply clauses in the same sentence are not a second M6 mark. Record, matching, not a second mark: Tenant Protection Bylaw on the Record page; 30 Jul 2026 council unanimously enhanced compensation (press 31 Jul 2026) and Dell is quoted that "continuing to approve rental developments will have a bigger impact on helping renters." M9c is struck; 26°C is gated — a May 2026 heat motion is not scored in this cluster. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) · [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/compensation-hiked-for-long-term-victoria-tenants-displaced-by-development-12613134](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/compensation-hiked-for-long-term-victoria-tenants-displaced-by-development-12613134) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · vote 30 Jul 2026 / press 31 Jul 2026
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — No published algorithmic waitlist, no by-name / HIFIS sentence in Dell's own name this pass. Loughton's HIFIS file is not a Dell sentence. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Approved 517 units of shelter and supportive housing for individuals experiencing homelessness." No Housing First target, no STEP throughput, no quarterly count. No 2026 Dell-owned Housing First sentence. Shown, not scored. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) — Childcare spaces, family-doctor recruitment and the 18–25 cohort do not appear. Parent / Little League / PAC background is not a source. M13 school food is \$0 and is not scored here. — —
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — Schools and SD61 do not appear. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Started the OUR DWTN program, which invests nearly \$900,000 annually into downtown cleanliness, safety and cultural events." No 2026 "continue OUR DWTN" sentence (unlike Loughton). No 90% graffiti standard, no sanitation hours. Shown, not scored. Arts/events in the same Record bullet are not a second M50 mark. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) **Partial 1.0** "Expand clean and active transportation options and public transit - so everyone can get around Victoria easily and at reasonable cost." · Commits to active transportation. Neither: no adaptive-signal programme, no Vision Zero audit, no named corridor. Transit in the same sentence is not a second M20b/M23b mark. Record AAA cycling / bike share / bike valet is matching context, not a second mark. M39 is struck — not scored. A 2023 speed-camera motion Dell seconded is Record context on this cluster, not a 2026 instrument and not scored again. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls **Partial 1.0** "Invest in streets, sidewalks & infrastructure." · Commits to sidewalk and street investment. Neither: no sidewalk-gap standard and no City-controlled transit-lever list. Distinct home-page bullet from the active-transportation sentence on row 27. "Fix roads first" sequencing is row 30, not here. "Walkable" on other bullets is branding and is not scored again. [https://www.mattdell.ca/](https://www.mattdell.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Committed \$14 million dollars to rebuild every public washroom in Victoria." No 2026 washroom-count or accessibility-audit sentence. No named Dell yes/no opened this pass. Shown, not scored. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
30 M25 fix roads first — The streets/sidewalks bullet is scored on row 28. That is investment, not a maintenance-backlog or roads-first sequencing rule. Mention of streets is not M25. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Supported funding for a business-security fund, a facade improvement fund, and a Douglas street revitalization fund." No named Dell yes/no opened this pass. Downtown-business 2026 sentence is scored on row 18. Shown, not scored. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
32 M28d community paramedicine — Community paramedicine is not named. CREST membership is a seat held, not a source. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) — No Dell-owned 2026 VicPD-formula or convene-and-publish sentence. FLAG: CHEK 3 Mar 2026 names four opposed to the 4→2 officer motion (Gardiner, Hammond, Coleman, Alto). Dell is not named. Do not invent a roll-call. Budget-day police spend is inside the M66 vote on row 13, not a second mark. — —
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting and the surveillance limit do not appear. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — CSWB is a plan, not a published safety KPI dashboard or crime-reduction number. Launch "community safety" is a Mention. Dash. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues **Close 2.0** "To do this, we must implement strategies in cooperation with the arts community, preserve important venues and provide grant funding for diverse artists to create work for the public." · Commits to cultural-venue preservation. Comparable, not Same: heritage standards and a street-furniture programme are not named. Grant funding in the same sentence is not a second M50 mark. Record, matching, not a second mark: "purchased Hermann's Jazz Club to ensure there's a place for arts and music downtown" (VicNews launch 31 Dec 2025 / Victoria Buzz 5 Jan 2026). Royal and McPherson board seat is a seat held, not a source. Not a sourced miss, so no Close cap. FLAG: a reader could argue Partial 1.0 because heritage standards are absent; ambiguity resolves upward. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) · [https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/](https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · launch 31 Dec 2025
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project 📋 Record Campaign Record page: "Supported pedestrianized areas across the city, including lower Government Street and other neighbourhood led spaces." No 2026 pedestrian-priority or signature-project sentence. "Walkable neighbourhoods" on the home page is branding, not pedestrianisation. Shown, not scored. [https://www.mattdell.ca/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) retrieved 2026-09-02
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks **Partial 1.0** "We need to preserve green space and invest in new parks with inclusive amenities, and we must invest in recreation facilities for everyone – such as a new Crystal Pool and Central Library." · Commits to new parks investment. Neither: no heritage-incentive schedule, no ornamental-lighting programme. Crystal Pool in this sentence is context; the dated 2030 completion is scored on row 39. FLAG: home-page "more parks & trees" is a different sentence, scored on row 49. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor **Partial 1.0** "Finish Crystal Pool by 2030." · Commits to a recreation-facility completion date. Neither: no arts-funding-floor percentage. Context, not a second mark: home-page "More events like Symphony Splash and Fernfest" / "Champion arts and culture"; grant-funding clause already used on row 36. City referendum 8 Feb 2025 is a voter result, not a named Dell vote. Unanimous site-endorsement press does not name Dell this pass — do not invent a roll-call. [https://www.mattdell.ca/](https://www.mattdell.ca/) · [https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/elections/crystal-pool-referendum](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/elections/crystal-pool-referendum) plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · referendum 8 Feb 2025
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — No published position. Absence of a managed-competition vote is Record, not Opposed. (Live-profile ❌ on this cell was already removed in v1.8 for having no source.) — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews — Budget-vote sentence is scored on row 13. No zero-based cycle, no grant test, no three-part test. — —
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard — "I commit to working to improve transparency, accessibility, and trust at City Hall" names transparency with no KPI set, no cadence, no dashboard. Mentions dash every column. Used as context on row 51, not here. — —
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — City real-estate holdings do not appear. Hermann's acquisition is scored on row 36 as a cultural venue, not as a holdings review. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — GIS, consultation imagery and LIDAR do not appear in any 2026 Dell-owned sentence this pass. Grade-breakdown AI marks are not a 2026 campaign source. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — No published municipal AI-governance standard. Same as the live-profile gap note. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement, open data, Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. Zero-emission / Step-code language is climate, scored on row 48. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic **Partial 1.0** "Advocate for policies that promote green building technologies, reduce waste and move towards a circular economy." · Commits to a municipal climate/building instrument. Neither: not the 50% / 2030 target set, not district energy, not seismic. Context, same policies section, not scored separately: "I am committed to doing everything possible to reduce emissions in Victoria." Record Climate Leadership Plan update / Zero Carbon Step-code is matching context, not a second mark. "Climate leadership stated" as a characterisation is not a source. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness **Partial 1.0** "Climate-smart city with more parks & trees." · Commits to more trees. Neither: no 5,000-tree target, no 35% canopy in the 2026 bullet, no emergency-preparedness position. Record page "Committed to a 40% Urban Tree canopy by 2050 (up from 30%)" is matching context, not a second mark. Mode share sits inside the sentence already scored on row 27. FLAG: parks also appear on row 38 from a different sentence. [https://www.mattdell.ca/](https://www.mattdell.ca/) retrieved 2026-09-02
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule — No \$25M threshold, 5-step sequence or material-change rule. Crystal Pool is scored on row 39 as a completion date, not as a referendum rule. The 8 Feb 2025 voter result is not a threshold position. — —
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response — "I support many of the recommendations for improved governance from the 2022 report, namely listening to residents and being transparent in making decisions." Names transparency. No Integrity Commissioner and no 60-day consultation-response standard. Mention, so a dash. The 2022 report was not opened this pass as containing those instruments. — —
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration — No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee position, no remuneration rule. — —
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans **Close 2.0** "We can do this by creating innovative local plans, in consultation with communities, to ensure each neighbourhood is unique, walkable and vibrant." · Commits to local plans with community consultation. Comparable, not Same: language-access and a neighbourhood-grant line are not named. "Walkable" in the same sentence is not a second M20b/M45b mark. Fernwood / James Bay liaison on the City biography is a seat held, not a source. Not a sourced miss, so no Close cap. FLAG: a reader could argue Partial 1.0 (local plans ≠ the Local Area Plan programme) or Aligned 3.0 (same instrument); ambiguity between Partial and Close resolves upward to Close, not to Aligned, because the rest of the cluster is absent. [https://www.mattdell.ca/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) retrieved 2026-09-02
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — "Leadership that listens" / "I want to hear your ideas" is a campaign practice, not a City survey, advance-vote or ballot-access instrument. Mention, so a dash. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) **Partial 1.0** "Councillors Chris Coleman, Matt Dell, Krista Loughton and Susan Kim sided with the mayor" to put "Do you support Saanich and Victoria becoming one municipality?" on the ballot, 5–4. Record-only hit vs M81. No 2026 Dell-owned execute-amalgamation sentence (unlike Loughton's "structural framework to execute it"). Not Close/Aligned. Policies page is silent on amalgamation. [https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-to-go-ahead-with-non-binding-amalgamation-question-12476505](https://www.timescolonist.com/local-news/victoria-to-go-ahead-with-non-binding-amalgamation-question-12476505) vote 25 Jun 2026 / press 27 Jun 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **Sources read in full:** [mattdell.ca](https://www.mattdell.ca/) home · [/policies](https://www.mattdell.ca/policies) · [/record](https://www.mattdell.ca/record) · [/about](https://www.mattdell.ca/about) (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [Victoria News launch 31 Dec 2025](https://vicnews.com/2025/12/31/victoria-coun-matt-dell-launches-his-bid-for-re-election-to-council/) · [Victoria Buzz 5 Jan 2026](https://victoriabuzz.com/2026/01/matt-dell-announces-plans-to-run-for-re-election-as-victoria-city-councillor/) · Times Colonist Missing Middle 27 Jan 2023, daytime sheltering 19 Jul 2024, budget 9 May 2026, amalgamation 27 Jun 2026, tenant compensation 31 Jul 2026 · Storeys Missing Middle 27 Jan 2023 · [City biography](https://www.victoria.ca/city-government/mayor-and-council/councillor-matt-dell) · [ACTW live profile](https://acitythatworks.ca/profiles/dell) · City budget page · Crystal Pool referendum page. Citified 2023 Q&A fetch timed out; 2023 text would be Record only, not a 2026 Plan cell. - **Searched and not found as a filled 2026 Dell-owned page:** VoteMate 2026 (no filled Dell profile opened this pass; 2022 VoteMate is Record only). No 2026 personal platform PDF. - **Not a source, applied:** Ministry of Finance / post-secondary civil-service career; musician / Kincaide / Croatia / Big Tree Band; South Jubilee presidency; Little League / PAC / Threshold run; Victoria Labour Council endorsement (third-party); Fernwood / James Bay liaison and CREST / Harbour Authority / Royal McPherson seats (seats held); 9,000-units campaign figure; "lowest of most surrounding cities" comparative tax frame; "pro-reconciliation" / "pro-bike" / "climate leadership stated" characterisations. - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Fourteen sentences carry the fourteen scored cells: (1) speed up rental / affordable / social / market housing → row 1. (2) strengthen policies to protect renters → row 21. (3) expand active transportation / public transit → row 27. (4) invest in streets, sidewalks & infrastructure → row 28. (5) preserve important venues → row 36. (6) invest in new parks → row 38. (7) Finish Crystal Pool by 2030 → row 39. (8) advocate green building / circular economy → row 48. (9) climate-smart city with more parks & trees → row 49. (10) budget YES 9.34% residential → row 13. (11) more supports for local business and tourism → row 18.
